explanation: The first patriarch with whom God made a covenant, father of Isaac and ancestor of the Jewish people.
Son of Abraham and Sarah, the second of the three great patriarchs in the Old Testament.
Son of Isaac who was named Israel; he was the father of twelve sons who became the founders of the twelve tribes of Israel.
The famous king over Israel and Judah, known for his victory over Goliath and his authorship in the Book of Psalms.
Son and successor of David, renowned for his wisdom and for building the first temple in Jerusalem.
Babylon; the place where the Jews were taken into captivity during the Babylonian exile before returning.
Mary's lawful husband, a righteous man who accepted Jesus and protected him from Herod's persecution.
The virgin who gave birth to Jesus by the Holy Spirit; she was married to Joseph from Nazareth in Galilee.
The Nazarene; God's Son, the Messiah (Christ) who was born of Mary and is the central figure in Christianity.
The Hebrew word for "the anointed one"; the title of the expected Savior who would rescue Israel from sin and oppression.
